notes.title: Devlog #6
notes.content:
As you may have noticed, we now have a special icon for our Devlogs with a joke inside (you could say, it's practically a single-frame comic)! But we also have other things to share with you today.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/fc8be6e7cc6ac083406d7aa5aa47f4c383690fbc.png[/img]
[h1]30,000 wishlists[/h1]
Not too long ago, we celebrated a very important milestone—25,000 wishlists on Steam. And in the blink of an eye, we've passed the 30,000 mark! Our recent trailer has been added to YouTube recommendations, garnering over 100,000 views in just one week.
 
[previewyoutube=Q4HWsqDoTz0;full][/previewyoutube]
We've received a tremendous amount of super-motivating feedback, and now even more people are waiting for the release of Princess Hunter. Thank you all for your support and trust!
[h1]Keeper of the Cold Spring[/h1]
Those of you who follow our project on [url=https://www.reddit.com/user/An_Dant]Reddit[/url], [url=https://twitter.com/Princessshunter]X[/url], or elsewhere, know that we drew this character last year. But now he's actually in the game! 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/f2242c0f56aa52f6f0892608eb714c006a0d8554.jpg[/img]
Lota's age is anyone's guess, as are his real thoughts. Despite his youthful appearance, he remembers Wyrdwood long before the arrival of Crimson King's hordes. His smile is more than just cold—it is icy!
[h1]Level building[/h1]
Although Princess Hunter looks like a cartoon, it is not as flat as it may seem. Frankly speaking, what you see is actually somewhere between a traditional 2D image and a 3D scene. This is called 2.5D, and it allows for deeper levels and opens up a lot of new possibilities… but it also creates just as many problems when building a level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/211e5ee00c2457014dc5e40cdb2e037f0726dfbf.png[/img]
To make life easier for level designers, our programmer has created a level building toolkit. Each scene now has several separate depth layers where you can sort objects both manually and automatically. In addition, it is now more convenient to plot the character's path. And for more thorough testing, it is possible to change the time scale by either speeding it up or slowing it down.

notes.title: Devlog #4
notes.content:
It's been a while since our last news update, but not because there was nothing worth writing about. We've been busy preparing a build for our new trailer which we really want to share with you just before this year ends or soon after the new year begins!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/9436f103588c68f6cc7bc59b44c98f43cd16e604.png[/img]

We've set ourselves a task not to create just a video reel, but to include as much real-game footage as possible into it, so that you could see what the game really looks and plays like. Therefore, our main goal was to make the latest build both atmospheric and pleasing to the eye.

[h1]Reflections[/h1]

There are plenty of various pools in Wyrdwood—one location is even called the "Lake Valley"! Up until now they've been providing the lush greenery with water, but still looked too static and dull. Not anymore!

[img]https://i.ibb.co/Wvx8bpw/Reflections2.gif[/img]

We proudly present revamped water to you, full of life, motion, and reflections! We've even written a special shader, and now water matches the style of other graphics in [b]Princess Hunter.[/b]  

[h1]Critters[/h1]

Surely, our plans to make the surroundings look more alive went beyond water. We decided to populate Wyrdwood not only with dangerous enemies and talkative NPCs, but with ordinary animals as well.

[img]https://i.ibb.co/kKf7Bg4/Critters.gif[/img]

Currently, the list of animals comprises several types of amphibians, some birds (including a cute-as-hell goatsucker), and a bunch of butterflies. These butterflies vary in color and even can follow pretty complicated flight paths.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/da62d585d223cf9645bbce6502865b41b4595d0d.jpg[/img]

We're planning to increase the biodiversity of forest life and even add some interactivity to it!

[h1]The Camp[/h1]

The campfire scene, however, took the most time. In static form, we made it a long time ago, but it still lacked an animated campfire and characters around it. Besides, we wanted to add real lighting.

This last task proved to be a tough one, since we were not satisfied with the quality of ready-made solutions for 2D scenes. That's why we had to experiment here, too, and write new shaders that would suit our needs. As has been mentioned above, it took us really much time, but the end result exceeded our expectations!

[img]https://i.ibb.co/jht6jf6/Camp2.gif[/img]

This illumination (all frames have been drawn by hand and have gone through many iterations) gave us the opportunity to see the camp in a completely new light ;) Add to this a gorgeous background music written specifically for this scene, and it would seem as if you really could feel the wavering warmth and smell the smoke.

notes.title: Devlog #3
notes.content:
[h1]Achievement Unlocked[/h1]

A year ago, when launching a Steam page for our game, we couldn't even imagine that the story of a Gunslinger traveling with a group of monstergirls would generate such a following. And we're proud to announce that recently we've reached our target of 10,000 wishlists! What's more, we've even surpassed it; currently, more than 12,000 people are looking forward to Princess Hunter's release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/e99d05877c0ce05b7a6327855f785d79976ead3f.png[/img]

It goes without saying that we find these figures highly motivating, which makes us redouble our efforts. We're extremely grateful to all of you who've added our game to your wishlists, told your friends about it, and—especially—signed up for updates like this Devlog. Thank you very much for putting your faith in us!

[h1]A New Character[/h1]

The Multiverse is inhabited by all sorts of sentient beings. Some of them have witnessed events of eons ago, and some have literally just appeared before your own eyes. Like, for instance, this slightly confused but lovable and friendly kid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/955a616ddf8096c54982a9c948372513a77c5097.png[/img]

Strictly speaking, it will depend on you, the player, whether the little A-Lot'l becomes a veritable magical spring Guardian and whether he appears at all in the first place!

[h1]First Things First[/h1]

Making a game is not just about implementing its mechanics, but also about building a set of tools to implement them efficiently. If the tools are handy, not only does it speed up the creation of a virtual world, it is also good for optimization, significantly reducing the number of bugs and facilitating the debugging process.

Specifically, our lead programmer has made a special Entry Level scene that initializes all in-game scripts in a given order. Before, all of this used to happen rather out of control, which introduced many unnecessary complications into the debugging process and could potentially become a game-breaker. Well, not anymore!

[h1]Traveling Between Levels[/h1]

And we've made progress in the game mechanics as well. In our previous devlog, we boasted that the Gunslinger can draw maps of places he'd visited—despite not being able to travel between them! Well, now he can do that too. The Gunslinger is no longer confined to a single location and may roam freely around Wyrdwood.

notes.title: Devlog #2
notes.content:
[h1]Maps[/h1]
In order not to get lost while exploring the game's many levels, the hero will diligently map his travels in his journal, complete with environmental sketches and notes. This is what it looks like:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/0f40a5f01df3b24a53d3a711d4ce01642e50eed7.png[/img]

Newly discovered clearings and important notes will be automatically added as the game progresses. To accomplish this, we've written a script that stores object states (soon we're going to use it for tweaking the quest system). While there is still much to be done concerning the maps, they are not placeholder pics anymore!

[h1]Also...[/h1]

Thanks to the script mentioned in the previous devlog, we now can change sprites on the map. For instance, when the Gunslinger finds a camp spot for the first time, it will look abandoned. But after spending at least one night there, it will have a tent and a small fire.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/0472c3092e0134bbae8227bfb051c77dd437471b.png[/img]

We've also added a custom function into the Fungus plugin that is able to run any external interface—barter, smithing, or combat—right in the middle of a dialogue, thus giving us much more narrative freedom.

notes.title: Devlog #1
notes.content:
[h1]Introduction[/h1]
Making comics and running contests is good, but what about the game? To keep everyone, who is invested in our project, informed about the development process, we've decided to start this Devlog, a Princess Hunter-related diary of sorts. 

Recently, the proportion of Nikitas in the team has grown 30%. We were lucky; the new Nikita turned out to be a very cool programmer. Thanks to him, the development process will hopefully gain an increased momentum. But before diving into the project proper, one has to study it first. That's why we asked him to implement an auxiliary, but still very interesting task, namely…
[h1]NOTES[/h1]
All worlds of Princess Hunter are inhabited by book gnomes. They can't read, but they have a bizarre attraction to handwritten texts. Gnomes fanatically steal every piece of paper or parchment they find, hiding them like squirrels hide nuts. It can be a page from a diary, a treasure map, a love letter, or a scrap from the Necronomicon. Well, you know... gnomes!

[img]https://i.ibb.co/3FMggTx/Dev-Log1-6.gif[/img]

Now our hero can pick up those notes and store them in his Journal. Some notes can be flipped, revealing extra texts (and drawings) on the reverse side. We've made five different variations of the notes to give each scrap of paper a unique look.

Meanwhile, the other part of the team was busy trying to harness…
[h1]EMOTIONS[/h1]
Dialogues are an essential part of Princess Hunter, and we relentlessly work on improving all their aspects.

The dialogue system uses the Unity plugin called Fungus, but over the course of development we've made a lot of major custom additions to it. As a result, Fungus has added many new features… but lost some original ones (which was quite unexpected). One of them was swapping character sprites during a dialogue: if the Gunslinger offends one of his companions, for example.

We couldn't accept such a loss, and that's why we wrote our own implementation of said feature. Now, nothing would prevent Ingeborg from becoming angrier or even enraged!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42647373/f142d10a2d2fdbf71bcdaa4a4bef289f81404f7c.png[/img]
